title: Rate-aware microbatch floorplan and KV reclamation policy
creator: Maria Chen
description:
Background:
Under sustained high QPS we observe pathological behavior where the continuous batcher aggressively accumulates tokens for latency-optimized models, leading to GPU memory headroom exhaustion and large KV cache churn. Existing backpressure thresholds are static and tuned for median loads; they either let microsurges fill GPU memory (causing OOMs or host-side shedding) or are conservative and hurt p95 latency.

Goal:
Design and implement a rate-aware microbatch "floorplan" (dynamic admission caps per model/route) plus an opportunistic KV reclamation policy that: 1) prevents GPU memory pressure-induced OOMs during long-tail QPS spikes, 2) preserves tail latency for latency-sensitive routes, and 3) enforces fairness across tenants and model variants when capacity is constrained.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Rate-aware floorplan: compute per-route microbatch admission caps computed from a combination of recent QPS (short window), per-token memory cost, and model-configured tail-latency SLA. Caps are expressed as "soft" microbatch size ceilings + a short burst allowance tied to token-window headroom.
- Adaptive backpressure thresholds: transform static floor thresholds into three watermarks (green/yellow/red) with hysteresis. Green = normal, allocate as usual. Yellow = slow down admission by adding inter-microbatch sleep and reducing target microbatch size. Red = reject or reroute to lower-cost variant.
- KV reclamation policy: implement an LRU-eviction with priority hints and a fast low-latency sweep triggered at yellow watermark. Priority hints: pinned prefixes (hot sessions) get a score boost; ephemeral or failed requests get low score. The sweep uses async eviction to avoid blocking inference threads.
- Fairness and tenant isolation: per-tenant fair share on microbatch slots computed using weighted deficit round-robin over admission tokens. When aggregate demand exceeds global capacity, lower-priority tenants receive proportional reduction.
- Simulation-first tuning: build a micro-simulator that replays production traffic traces (from last-month p95/p99 bursts) to tune watermarks and burst allowances before rolling out.

Design trade-offs and decisions:
- Why three watermarks vs two: three levels let us introduce low-cost mitigation (yellow) without immediate user-visible rejection. This reduces false positives during transient jitter.
- Async eviction vs sync: async eviction avoids stalling the GPU path, but may temporarily increase memory pressure. We'll limit concurrent async evictors and expose metrics to ensure the sweep completes fast enough.
- Per-route config surface: expose recommended defaults and allow ops to override per-customer. Too much configurability risks misconfiguration; we will gate per-route overrides behind Dedicated/Private tiers initially.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) RFC + simulation harness (complete) — design doc: https://confluence.redwood/inference/rate-aware-floorplan-rfc (internal)
2) Simulator runs and recommended thresholds (complete) — benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood/inference/microbatch-sim/26789
3) Admission controller prototype (PR-1) — microbatch admission module with green/yellow/red states, unit tests and integration tests (in review) GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4582
4) KV reclamation async sweep (PR-2) — eviction worker + priority hints + metrics (in progress) GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4620
5) Canary rollout to staging + loadtests (planned)
6) Gradual prod rollout with canary rules per-region (planned)

Observability and alerts:
- New metrics: microbatch_admissions{route,state}, kv_reclaim_rate, kv_eviction_latency_p50_p95_p99, gpu_host_memory_headroom_bytes, admission_rejection_count.
- Dashboards: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency vs admission cap, headroom over time, kv-eviction activity overlay.
- Alerts: headroom < 10% sustained for 30s -> page on-call; admission_rejection_rate > 1% and customer_impact=high -> page SEs.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for admission logic and state transitions (green->yellow->red).
- Integration test: synthetic replay with recorded traces to validate no OOMs and acceptable p95 degradation (<10% over baseline).
- Staging canary: 3 nodes, replay high-QPS trace at 2x. Monitor kv_eviction_rate and gpu headroom.
- Gradual canary in prod: region-by-region with automatic rollback threshold on elevated rejection rate or p99 latency > baseline + 20%.

Open questions / risks:
- Edge-case of long-lived pinned KV prefixes consuming disproportionate memory. Mitigation: allow manual pin eviction and admin-only pressure-reclaim.
- Interaction with quantized model variants: smaller KV entries but more kernels, need perf balance. Add model-specific cost multipliers.
- Fairness algorithm tuning complexity; will require iterative calibration with production telemetry.

Deliverables:
- Admission controller module and config schema (runtime-1.24)
- Async KV reclamation worker with priority hints
- Simulator + tuning config and dashboards
- Runbook for on-call + rollback criteria

References and artifacts:
- Simulator repo: https://git.internal.redwood/sim/microbatch-sim (internal)
- Design RFC: https://confluence.redwood/inference/rate-aware-floorplan-rfc
- PR-1: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4582
- PR-2: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4620
- Loadtest dashboards: https://dash.redwood/inference/microbatch-loadtests

Next steps (short term):
- Merge PR-1 after addressing review comments (blocked on metric naming and an additional unit test for hysteresis).
- Finish KV reclaim worker PR and add async-evict metrics (ETA 2026-03-12).
- Run staging canary by 2026-03-15.
